newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan bankers' head not concerned about recovery.
newsitem.headline: Japan bankers' head not concerned about recovery.

text.p: Shunsaku Hashimoto, chairman of the Federation of Bankers' Associations of Japan, said on Tuesday he was not worried about Japan's economy even though the pace of its recovery has slowed recently.
"The economy has been slowly recovering, although the speed of the recovery has been slowing down since the summer," Hashimoto told a regular news conference.
"I am not worried about a downturn in the economy... I expect the economy to continue recovering slowly," he said.
Hashimoto, also president of Sakura Bank Ltd, said he wanted the government to review and expand the range of businesses which banks' securities units can engage in.

"As president of a commercial bank, I want (the government) to expand the range of business the banks' securities arms can engage in, to relax regulations on the arms and to allow banks to start over-the-counter sales of investment trust products," Hashimoto said.
Financial reforms which took effect in April 1993 allowed banks and brokerages to set up fully owned subsidiaries in each other's turf.
However, the Finance Ministry decided not to allow banks' securities subsidiaries to engage in stock business so as not to jeopardise existing stock brokers.
